english.title: Failed to deliver return by end of withdrawal period being liable for tax on offshore income, assets or activities
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), were required by a notice under section 8 of the Taxes Management Act 1970 to make and deliver a return for a year of assessment, namely **(..SPECIFY ASSESSMENT YEAR..), which was not delivered by **(..SPECIFY END OF THE WITHDRAWAL PERIOD..), the end of the withdrawal period, when an accurate return would have disclosed liability to

(A)_[income tax]_
(B)_[capital gains tax]_
(C)_[income tax and capital gains tax]_

that was chargeable for that year on or by reference to offshore income, assets or activities, and the total amount of income tax and capital gains tax that was chargeable for the year of assessment on or by such reference exceeded the threshold amount
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 106C(1) and 106G of the Taxes Management Act 1970.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Under section 106C(2) it is a defence for a person accused of an offence under this section to prove that the person had a reasonable excuse for failing to give the notice required by section 7.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 monthsNote
When section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 6 months is to be read as a reference to 51 weeks.
